caption: The drawing depicts detailed orthographic projections of a chair, referred to as a "Dutch Chair" from 1720-1730, located in the South Parlor of Wetherfield House and noted as made from cherry wood. The composition includes four main outlined views on a pale, off-white background: a front view, back view, side view, and top view. The front and back views show a high-backed chair with a central vertical split in the backrest, featuring two symmetrically curved vertical splats. The legs in the front and back views have outward curving cabriole shapes, with crossbars connecting them for structural support. The side view illustrates the profile of the chair, highlighting the curved profile of the backrest and the legs with the same cabriole styling. The top view shows the seat's contours, which has a slightly rounded front and a more squared back, measuring 20 inches across. The drawing is rendered in fine black lines with measurements and construction details marked in light red; dimensions, such as seat height and backrest height, are noted beside the parts. Handwritten text is present on the drawing, providing the object's historical context, material, scale (1/8" = 1'), and the draftsman's name and museum affiliation.
title: Drawing for Chair
